key_insight: Introduce a differentiable reward flow (Diffusion-DRF) that lets gradients from preference/reward signals propagate back into video diffusion models, enabling stable, label-efficient fine-tuning and reducing reward-hacking.
problem_solved: Current T2V fine-tuning relies on non-differentiable human labels or learned reward models, which is label-intensive, bias-prone, and susceptible to reward hacking and unstable training dynamics.
method: Design a differentiable reward flow that estimates preferences in a way that is backpropagatable through the diffusion sampling/fine-tuning pipeline.
Integrate the differentiable reward with a DPO-style objective to directly optimize video diffusion models for visual fidelity and text alignment without non-differentiable reward signals.
Train with fewer human annotations and greater stability, mitigating reward-hacking by keeping the reward pathway differentiable and aligned with generation gradients.
impact: Makes video diffusion fine-tuning more robust, data-efficient, and harder to game — enabling practitioners to improve text-to-video fidelity and alignment with fewer labels and more stable training.

paper_title: Diffusion-DRF: Differentiable Reward Flow for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
